top_signals.title: Stocks Drop as Risk-Off Views Dominate With Oil Up, Meta Falling
top_signals.summary: Stocks opened lower on Thursday as escalating concern about Mideast conflict pushed oil futures higher, spurring inflation fears with US midterm elections less than two weeks away. Meta Platforms Inc. tumbled as investors parsed its results along with the rest of the latest batch of technology earnings for evidence that massive spending on AI is paying off.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Commodity repricing impacting inflation expectations and industrial supply chains.

top_signals.title: Copper’s AI Tailwind Faces Supply and Demand Uncertainty
top_signals.summary: At LME week, Amy Gower of Morgan Stanley said copper traders lack conviction about the metal’s direction. Copper has tracked AI stocks closely, although AI is still a small share of demand; uncertainty over possible U.S. import tariffs is also drawing large volumes of copper into the country and could redirect supply from other markets. Gower said mine supply is expected to fall this year, with further risks next year from project recoveries and potential strikes in Chile and the U.S. Other possible supports include continued tariff-related stockpiling, stronger AI demand and Chinese stimulus. But China’s end-use indicators are mixed, and weakness in construction and property remains a concern. The discussion also noted that copper’s recent gains are struggling to extend. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.
